clue.text: Watson went down. Dean of Christ Church didn't appeal

parts.note: Sherlock Holmes's companion is Dr Watson, so a doctor
to fall is to go down, past tense fell

explanation.surface: Holmes's friend collapses while a college dean leaves everyone cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Didn't appeal' alludes to the rhyme 'I do not love thee, Dr Fell', written about John Fell, Dean of Christ Church, Oxford.
explanation.definitionFit: John Fell was the seventeenth-century Oxford dean mocked in the famous rhyme of dislike.

clue.text: What an apprentice pirate, its slave, had to do

definitions.text: What an apprentice pirate, its slave, had to do

parts.words: What an apprentice pirate, its slave, had to do
parts.note: in Gilbert and Sullivan's Pirates of Penzance, Frederic, apprenticed to pirates, is 'the slave of' this obligation

explanation.surface: A trainee buccaneer's grim obligations.
explanation.definitionFit: Frederic in The Pirates of Penzance is subtitled the Slave of moral obligation.

clue.text: Century scored by a little girl

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
to hit is to score, as in hitting a target

explanation.surface: A small girl makes a hundred at cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: A century is a hundred runs in cricket, so the surface pictures a girl batting.
explanation.definitionFit: Chit is old-fashioned slang for a pert young girl.

clue.text: One approaching the naughty age?

parts.note: 'naughty' read as 'nought-y', a person nearing the decade that ends in nought, i.e. ninety

explanation.surface: A child close to the age for misbehaving.
explanation.definitionFit: A person in their eighties is nearing ninety, the 'nought-y' age.

clue.text: Patrons of pugilism? Imagine that!

definitions.meaning: the old collective name for followers of prize-fighting

explanation.surface: Boxing fans express surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Regency boxing followers were 'the Fancy'; the exclamation is also used to express surprise.

clue.text: Men talk in odd angles about the half-month's return

indicators.note: the scrambled letters go about, around, the other piece
the piece comes back, read backwards

parts.note: the first half of August, a summer month

explanation.surface: People chat at strange angles about a fortnight coming back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd' makes LANGES (ANGLES rearranged) and 'about' puts it round GUA, which 'return' makes from AUG.
explanation.definitionFit: People speak in various tongues, such as French or Welsh.

clue.text: Milton's fame to boot

explanation.surface: A poet's renown comes as a bonus.
explanation.definitionFit: Milton's Lycidas says 'Fame is the spur' that drives the mind; a rider's spur is strapped to the boot.

clue.text: Apostrophized in an anarchist's "A plague on both your houses!"?

definitions.text: Apostrophized in an anarchist's "A plague on both your houses!"?

parts.words: Apostrophized in an anarchist's "A plague on both your houses!"?
parts.note: Mercutio's curse borrowed by an anarchist, addressed to the legislature's Lords and Commons

explanation.surface: Mercutio's curse quoted by a revolutionary.
explanation.definitionFit: Westminster's legislature has two chambers, Lords and Commons, both cursed together.

clue.text: Wild gorse over the forest provides a floral setting

indicators.note: in a down clue this piece is placed over, above, the next
wild letters run free and rearrange themselves

parts.note: the Forest of Arden, in Warwickshire and Shakespeare's As You Like It

explanation.surface: Wild shrubs above the woodland make a flowery scene.
explanation.definitionFit: A flowerbed area of roses is a floral setting.

clue.text: Steps taken by a writer (not of these articles)

definitions.text: Steps taken by a writer (not of these articles)

parts.words: Steps taken by a writer (not of these articles)
parts.note: a number shared by John Buchan's spy novel about steps and the Church of England's articles of religion; the clue keeps the novel and rejects the articles

explanation.surface: An author's procedure, distinct from some printed items.
explanation.walkthrough: John Buchan wrote the thriller about the steps; the Church of England's doctrinal Articles have the same count, which the bracket rules out.
explanation.definitionFit: Buchan's novel title gives a count of steps, the same count as the Anglican Articles of Religion.

clue.text: Flag girl

definitions.meaning: flag is a name for the yellow wild plant of riverbanks with sword leaves

explanation.surface: A girl waving a banner.
explanation.definitionFit: The yellow flag is a wild species of this bulb plant, and it is also a woman's name.

clue.text: Under full complement do they fly the Jolly Roger ?

definitions.text: Under full complement do they fly the Jolly Roger

parts.words: Under full complement do they fly the Jolly Roger
parts.note: a reduced ship's company sounds like a crew of skulls and bones, who might hoist the pirate flag

explanation.surface: Does a short-handed ship hoist the pirate flag?
explanation.definitionFit: A minimal team running something is a bare-bones crew, punning on the skull flag.

clue.text: Product of Hans Andersen's pen

parts.note: something the Danish storyteller wrote: his tale of an unlovely cygnet among farmyard birds

explanation.surface: Something the Danish author wrote.
explanation.definitionFit: Andersen's fairy tale tells of a homely young bird that grows into a swan.

clue.text: This lizard-like variety in Dar-es-Salaam is a dropout

indicators.note: a variety is a mixed assortment, so the letters are mixed
the words 'is a' drop out of the letter pool

explanation.surface: A lizard-like strain found in an African city has quit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variety' rearranges IN plus DARESSALAAM; 'dropout' removes the letters of IS A, leaving the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The amphibian with a tailed lizard shape is a newt-like creature.

clue.text: Poorest performer gets the bird

parts.note: the worst competitor receives the consolation award named after a seabird, the gannet's relative

explanation.surface: The weakest act is booed off stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets the bird' sounds like being jeered, but the bird is the booby.
explanation.definitionFit: A joke award for last place is named after a seabird.

clue.text: A spring that's copious

parts.note: to spring is to leap, so springing means leaping forward

explanation.surface: A water source that flows plentifully.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spring' looks like a noun, a water source, but works as a verb: springing along.
explanation.definitionFit: Something present in great plenty is copious, overflowing with supply.

clue.text: Tax top class engineer with fraud

parts.note: an impost is a tax or duty
U means upper class
RE is the Royal Engineers

explanation.surface: Levying the upper class with an engineer's help is a swindle.
explanation.definitionFit: Pretending to be someone else for deception is a fraud.

clue.text: Both sides accept a bird for, for instance, a bush-baby

indicators.note: the two sides take in, or accept, a piece between them

parts.note: L and R, left and right
the emu, a large flightless Australian bird

explanation.surface: Two parties welcome a bird on behalf of a small primate.
explanation.walkthrough: The bush-baby (galago) was long grouped with these primates, so it is an example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The bush-baby is a small nocturnal African primate of the prosimian group that also includes Madagascar's ring-tails.

clue.text: Red's predecessor at the crossroads

parts.note: on a British traffic light the colour shown just before red, at a junction

explanation.surface: Someone who held office before a radical leader at a turning point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Red' suggests a politician, but it is the traffic light: in Britain, red follows the orange-yellow light.
explanation.definitionFit: Traffic signals go green, then a yellowish warning light, then red.

clue.text: What was is, what is cannot be

definitions.text: What was is, what is cannot be

parts.words: What was is, what is cannot be
parts.note: the verb form 'was' belongs to a grammatical category for bygone time, which the present form 'is' cannot belong to

explanation.surface: A philosophical riddle about being and time.
explanation.definitionFit: Grammar names the verb form for completed time, such as 'was' or 'went'.

clue.text: Semi — apparent possibly in one's estimation

indicators.note: these letters could possibly be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Someone judges a thing only half visible.
explanation.definitionFit: A valuation or assessment of worth is an estimation.

clue.text: Modern chariot, last of it seen in Othello

indicators.note: the letter is seen within the other piece

parts.note: Shakespeare's Othello is the Moor of Venice

indicators.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A chariot finished off in Shakespeare's tragedy.
explanation.definitionFit: A car is a present-day chariot.

clue.text: Resort for leaders of Kremlin in Easter vacation ?

indicators.note: the leaders of these words are their initial letters

explanation.surface: Kremlin bosses holiday at a resort over Easter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ukrainian capital was a place to visit or holiday.

clue.text: On which X goes bottom over top in the Alps

definitions.text: On which X goes bottom over top in the Alps

parts.words: On which X goes bottom over top in the Alps
parts.note: a crossed pair of runners, shaped like X, sends the wearer tumbling head over heels in the mountains

explanation.surface: A downhill tumble in the mountains.
explanation.definitionFit: Long runners for snow travel cross into an X when a skier falls.

clue.text: Perry Mason's opponent is on the platform

parts.note: the TV defence lawyer always faces the District Attorney, the prosecutor
taken as written

explanation.surface: A courtroom adversary stands on the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A raised stand at the end of a hall is a platform.

clue.text: A dairy product, but same is out of period

indicators.note: the word for 'same' comes out of, that is follows on from, the period word

parts.note: taken as written
a term is a period of time, such as a school term
ilk means kind or sort, as in 'of that ilk', the same

explanation.surface: A dairy item that is out of season.
explanation.definitionFit: The sour liquid left after churning cream is a dairy product.

clue.text: Right fish on the rod

definitions.note: the definition is the thing that sits on a fishing rod, a winding device

parts.note: the eel is a snakelike fish

explanation.surface: The correct fish caught on a fishing line.
explanation.definitionFit: An angler's line winds onto the spool mounted on the rod.

clue.text: Playful ladies slightly tipsy ? Halves better

parts.note: merry is a British word for mildly drunk
'better halves' is a jocular name for spouses, here women

explanation.surface: Some women, a little drunk, are improved by halving.
explanation.walkthrough: Shakespeare's comedy has two playful ladies of Windsor; 'merry' is British for tipsy.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's Windsor comedy is about two married women who play tricks on Falstaff.
